### Universal_Seat_Twin.f90

~~~~~fortran file=Universal_Seat_Twin.f90
! Universal_Seat_Twin.f90 . the executed twin of Universal_Seat.lean.
! Every check is a finite computation that ends. Each law that could be coded as an identity runs beside a control
! in which it must fail, so a green line here is a check that could have been red. The lost bit is checked where it
! can fail: the registration, computed, sends both partners to one record; that no map returns both is then the
! consequence, printed and no pass condition. The zeros of the series are located by the twin, none supplied.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off
program universal_seat_twin
  use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: qp => real128, dp => real64
  implicit none
  integer :: nchk = 0, nfail = 0
  call seats()
  call both_partners()
  call two_definitions()
  call stream()
  call bridge()
  call floor_digit()
  call zeta_series()
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', nchk, ',"failures":', nfail, '}'
  if (nfail /= 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    nchk = nchk + 1
    if (.not. ok) nfail = nfail + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ', '  FAIL  ', ok), name
  end subroutine check
  ! the chart at grain n: the fold x to 2n - x, the registration onto x = n; grain 0 is the offset chart
  pure function foldg(n, p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: n, p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [2 * n - p(1), p(2)]
  end function foldg
  pure function regg(n, p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: n, p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [n, p(2)]
  end function regg
  pure integer function idx(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    idx = p(1) + 2 + 3 * p(2)
  end function idx
  pure logical function hasoff(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    hasoff = iand(m, 365) /= 0
  end function hasoff
  pure integer function recof(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: t
    recof = 0
    do t = 0, 2
      if (iand(m, ishft(7, 3 * t)) /= 0) recof = ibset(recof, t)
    end do
  end function recof

  ! I . the four laws of a seat, on five charts
  subroutine seats()
    integer :: gr(5), i, n, x, t, p(2)
    logical :: ok
    gr = [0, 1, 2, 6, 10]; ok = .true.
    do i = 1, 5
      n = gr(i)
      do x = n - 5, n + 5
        do t = 0, 3
          p = [x, t]
          if (any(foldg(n, foldg(n, p)) /= p)) ok = .false.
          if (any(foldg(n, regg(n, p)) /= regg(n, p))) ok = .false.
          if (all(foldg(n, p) == p) .and. any(regg(n, p) /= p)) ok = .false.
          if (any(regg(n, foldg(n, p)) /= regg(n, p))) ok = .false.
          if (all(regg(n, p) == p) .neqv. all(foldg(n, p) == p)) ok = .false.
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('I: the four laws of a seat hold on five charts, grains 0, 1, 2, 6 and 10, 220 points', ok)
  end subroutine seats

  ! II . one bit is lost. What can fail is checked: the two partners of a pair are distinct and the registration,
  ! computed, sends both to one record. From that alone no map returns both, so that count is printed as the
  ! consequence it is and is no pass condition. The live counts are the most recovered and the times one is.
  subroutine both_partners()
    integer :: g(6), m, k, i, t, mode, got, best(2), nboth(2), none_(2), nsame(2), ip, iq, rp, rq
    best = 0; nboth = 0; none_ = 0; nsame = 0
    do mode = 1, 2
      do t = 0, 1
        ip = idx([1, t]); iq = idx(foldg(0, [1, t]))
        if (mode == 1) then
          rp = idx(regg(0, [1, t])); rq = idx(regg(0, foldg(0, [1, t])))
        else
          rp = ip; rq = iq
        end if
        if (ip /= iq .and. rp == rq) nsame(mode) = nsame(mode) + 1
      end do
      do m = 0, 6**6 - 1
        k = m
        do i = 1, 6
          g(i) = mod(k, 6) + 1; k = k / 6
        end do
        do t = 0, 1
          ip = idx([1, t]); iq = idx(foldg(0, [1, t]))
          if (mode == 1) then
            rp = idx(regg(0, [1, t])); rq = idx(regg(0, foldg(0, [1, t])))
          else
            rp = ip; rq = iq
          end if
          got = 0
          if (g(rp) == ip) got = got + 1
          if (g(rq) == iq) got = got + 1
          best(mode) = max(best(mode), got)
          if (got == 2) nboth(mode) = nboth(mode) + 1
          if (got == 1) none_(mode) = none_(mode) + 1
        end do
      end do
    end do
    write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a,i0,a,i0)') '  pairs sent to one record ', nsame(1), ' of 2; most recovered ', best(1), &
         '; one member ', none_(1), ' times; both, the consequence, ', nboth(1)
    call check('II: both partners of each pair go to one record; over 46656 maps the most recovered is one, 31104 times', &
         nsame(1) == 2 .and. best(1) == 1 .and. none_(1) == 31104)
    call check('II: control, a registration that keeps the side: no pair shares a record; both recovered 2592 times', &
         nsame(2) == 0 .and. best(2) == 2 .and. nboth(2) == 2592)
  end subroutine both_partners

  ! III . the two definitions of least erasure against the value, the record's definition by search over every world
  subroutine two_definitions()
    integer :: m, mp, k, d, t, bad, badc
    logical :: val, ler, ext
    bad = 0; badc = 0
    do m = 0, 511
      val = .true.; ler = .true.
      do k = 0, 8
        if (btest(m, k)) then
          d = mod(k, 3) - 1; t = k / 3
          if (any(foldg(0, [d, t]) /= [d, t])) val = .false.
          if (any(regg(0, [d, t]) /= [d, t])) ler = .false.
        end if
      end do
      ext = .true.
      if (hasoff(m)) then
        do mp = 0, 511
          if (recof(mp) == recof(m) .and. .not. hasoff(mp)) ext = .false.
        end do
      end if
      if ((ext .neqv. val) .or. (ler .neqv. val)) bad = bad + 1
      if (iand(m, 146) == 0) then
        ext = .true.
        if (hasoff(m)) then
          do mp = 0, 511
            if (iand(mp, 146) == 0 .and. recof(mp) == recof(m) .and. .not. hasoff(mp)) ext = .false.
          end do
        end if
        if (ext .neqv. val) badc = badc + 1
      end if
    end do
    call check('III: the two definitions of least erasure and the value agree on all 512 worlds, by search', bad == 0)
    call check('III: control, the line removed from the universe: the record''s definition fails on 63 worlds', &
         badc == 63)
  end subroutine two_definitions

  ! IV . the stream: the value of a listed world is its bits; no shorter stretch decides
  subroutine digits(a, z)
    integer, intent(in) :: a
    integer, intent(out) :: z(0:5)
    integer :: n, k
    k = a
    do n = 0, 5
      z(n) = mod(k, 3) - 1; k = k / 3
    end do
  end subroutine digits
  logical function setvalue(z)
    integer, intent(in) :: z(0:5)
    logical :: inset(-1:1, 0:5)
    integer :: n, d
    inset = .false.
    do n = 0, 5
      inset(z(n), n) = .true.
    end do
    setvalue = .true.
    do n = 0, 5
      do d = -1, 1
        if (inset(d, n) .and. d /= 0) setvalue = .false.
      end do
    end do
  end function setvalue
  subroutine stream()
    integer :: a, b, k, n, za(0:5), zb(0:5), nbad
    logical :: va, vb, bits, found(0:6), agree
    nbad = 0; found = .false.
    do a = 0, 728
      call digits(a, za)
      va = setvalue(za); bits = .true.
      do n = 0, 5
        if (any(foldg(0, [za(n), n]) /= [za(n), n])) bits = .false.
      end do
      if (va .neqv. bits) nbad = nbad + 1
      do b = 0, 728
        call digits(b, zb); vb = setvalue(zb)
        if (va .eqv. vb) cycle
        do k = 0, 6
          agree = .true.
          do n = 0, k - 1
            if (za(n) /= zb(n)) agree = .false.
          end do
          if (agree) found(k) = .true.
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('IV: the value of a listed world is its bit-stream, on all 729 streams', nbad == 0)
    call check('IV: no stretch shorter than the stream decides, 0 to 5 members; the whole stream does', &
         all(found(0:5)) .and. .not. found(6))
  end subroutine stream

  ! V . the bridge of the charts, beside a shift that is off by one
  subroutine bridge()
    integer :: gr(4), i, n, x, t, p(2), a(2), b(2), fails(0:1), shift
    gr = [1, 2, 6, 10]; fails = 0
    do shift = 0, 1
      do i = 1, 4
        n = gr(i)
        do x = n - 5, n + 5
          do t = 0, 3
            p = [x, t]
            a = foldg(n, p); b = regg(n, p)
            if (any([a(1) - n + shift, a(2)] /= foldg(0, [x - n + shift, t])) .or. &
                any([b(1) - n + shift, b(2)] /= regg(0, [x - n + shift, t]))) fails(shift) = fails(shift) + 1
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('V: at grains 1, 2, 6 and 10 the shift by n carries fold and registration onto the offset chart', &
         fails(0) == 0)
    call check('V: control, a shift off by one: the conjugation fails at all 176 points', fails(1) == 176)
  end subroutine bridge

  ! VI . the floor's last digit
  subroutine floor_digit()
    real(qp) :: s, tail, lo, prod
    integer :: k
    s = 0.0_qp
    do k = 1, 60
      s = s + 1.0_qp / (real(k, qp) * 2.0_qp**k)
    end do
    tail = 1.0_qp / (60.0_qp * 2.0_qp**60)
    lo = 6931471805599453.0_qp / 1.0e16_qp
    call check('VI: the sixtieth partial sum lies above 0.6931471805599453 and, with its tail, below ...454', &
         lo < s .and. s + tail < lo + 1.0e-16_qp)
    prod = 1380649.0_qp * 300.0_qp * 6931471805599453.0_qp
    call check('VI: 1380649 x 300 x 6931471805599453 is 2870978885078723755499100, exact at sixteen places', &
         abs(prod - 2870978885078723755499100.0_qp) < 0.5_qp)
  end subroutine floor_digit

  ! VII . the series the kernel defines. First the finite sums of the kernel, in the arithmetic of this twin, held
  ! to the bracket the kernel proves (series_meet_the_twin). Then the inner limits, against the functions of the
  ! machine. Then the zeros, located by Newton iteration from starts off the line with no ordinate supplied; the
  ! tables are read afterwards, as corroboration. The acceleration is Cohen, Rodriguez Villegas, Zagier (2000).
  pure function expn(n, x) result(v)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(qp), intent(in) :: x
    real(qp) :: v, term
    integer :: k
    v = 1.0_qp; term = 1.0_qp
    do k = 1, n
      term = term * x / real(k, qp); v = v + term
    end do
  end function expn
  pure function cosn(n, x) result(v)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(qp), intent(in) :: x
    real(qp) :: v, term
    integer :: k
    v = 1.0_qp; term = 1.0_qp
    do k = 1, n
      term = -term * x * x / (real(2 * k - 1, qp) * real(2 * k, qp)); v = v + term
    end do
  end function cosn
  pure function sinn(n, x) result(v)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(qp), intent(in) :: x
    real(qp) :: v, term
    integer :: k
    v = x; term = x
    do k = 1, n
      term = -term * x * x / (real(2 * k, qp) * real(2 * k + 1, qp)); v = v + term
    end do
  end function sinn
  pure function lnn(n, m) result(v)
    integer, intent(in) :: n, m
    real(qp) :: v, y, p
    integer :: j
    y = real(m - 1, qp) / real(m + 1, qp); p = y; v = y
    do j = 1, n
      p = p * y * y; v = v + p / real(2 * j + 1, qp)
    end do
    v = 2.0_qp * v
  end function lnn
  ! etaRe and etaIm of the kernel: terms m = 1 .. mtop + 1, each at the n-th approximation
  subroutine eta_own(mtop, n, b, tt, re, im)
    integer, intent(in) :: mtop, n
    real(qp), intent(in) :: b, tt
    real(qp), intent(out) :: re, im
    integer :: j
    real(qp) :: l, a, sg
    re = 0.0_qp; im = 0.0_qp; sg = 1.0_qp
    do j = 0, mtop
      l = lnn(n, j + 1); a = expn(n, -(b * l))
      re = re + sg * a * cosn(n, tt * l); im = im - sg * a * sinn(n, tt * l)
      sg = -sg
    end do
  end subroutine eta_own
  ! the same sum with the inner limits taken by the functions of the machine
  subroutine eta_mach(mtop, b, tt, re, im)
    integer, intent(in) :: mtop
    real(qp), intent(in) :: b, tt
    real(qp), intent(out) :: re, im
    integer :: j
    real(qp) :: l, a, sg
    re = 0.0_qp; im = 0.0_qp; sg = 1.0_qp
    do j = 0, mtop
      l = log(real(j + 1, qp)); a = exp(-(b * l))
      re = re + sg * a * cos(tt * l); im = im - sg * a * sin(tt * l)
      sg = -sg
    end do
  end subroutine eta_mach
  ! the alternating series, summed with acceleration; own takes each term from the four series of the kernel at
  ! inner index nin, otherwise from the functions of the machine
  function eta_acc(s, nt, own, nin) result(e)
    complex(qp), intent(in) :: s
    integer, intent(in) :: nt, nin
    logical, intent(in) :: own
    complex(qp) :: e, acc, ak
    real(qp) :: d, b, c, l, a
    integer :: k
    real(qp), save :: lntab(64)
    integer, save :: ltn = -1
    if (own .and. ltn /= nin) then
      do k = 1, 64
        lntab(k) = lnn(nin, k)
      end do
      ltn = nin
    end if
    d = (3.0_qp + sqrt(8.0_qp))**nt; d = (d + 1.0_qp / d) / 2.0_qp
    b = -1.0_qp; c = -d; acc = cmplx(0.0_qp, 0.0_qp, qp)
    do k = 0, nt - 1
      c = b - c
      if (own) then
        l = lntab(k + 1); a = expn(nin, -(real(s, qp) * l))
        ak = cmplx(a * cosn(nin, aimag(s) * l), -(a * sinn(nin, aimag(s) * l)), qp)
      else
        ak = exp(-s * log(real(k + 1, qp)))
      end if
      acc = acc + c * ak
      b = real(k + nt, qp) * real(k - nt, qp) * b / ((real(k, qp) + 0.5_qp) * real(k + 1, qp))
    end do
    e = acc / d
  end function eta_acc
  function newton(s0, nt, own, nin, h, nit) result(s)
    complex(qp), intent(in) :: s0
    integer, intent(in) :: nt, nin, nit
    logical, intent(in) :: own
    real(qp), intent(in) :: h
    complex(qp) :: s, f, fp
    integer :: it
    s = s0
    do it = 1, nit
      f = eta_acc(s, nt, own, nin)
      fp = (eta_acc(s + h, nt, own, nin) - eta_acc(s - h, nt, own, nin)) / (2.0_qp * h)
      s = s - f / fp
    end do
  end function newton
  subroutine partial(b, tt, mtop, sre, sim)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: b, tt
    integer, intent(in) :: mtop
    real(dp), intent(out) :: sre, sim
    integer :: m
    real(dp) :: lg, a, sg
    sre = 0.0_dp; sim = 0.0_dp; sg = 1.0_dp
    do m = 1, mtop
      lg = log(real(m, dp)); a = exp(-b * lg)
      sre = sre + sg * a * cos(tt * lg); sim = sim - sg * a * sin(tt * lg)
      sg = -sg
    end do
  end subroutine partial
  subroutine zeta_series()
    real(qp), parameter :: lo_re = 0.53180207690295243439_qp, lo_im = 0.22737850912720984721_qp, w = 2.0e-20_qp
    real(qp), parameter :: tab(3) = [14.134725141734693790457251983562_qp, &
         21.022039638771554992628479593897_qp, 25.010857580145688763213790992563_qp]
    real(qp), parameter :: h0(3) = [14.0_qp, 21.0_qp, 25.0_qp]
    complex(qp) :: z(3), zo
    real(qp) :: re, im, re2, im2, rm, imm, dev8, dev60
    real(dp) :: sre, sim, r(3), off, t1
    integer :: mm(3), i
    logical :: ok
    call eta_own(2, 8, 0.5_qp, 2.0_qp, re, im)
    write(*,'(a,f24.20,a,f24.20)') '  the finite sum of the kernel at 1/2 + 2i, three terms, eight inner: ', re, ' ', im
    call check('VII: the kernel and the twin meet: the same finite sum lands inside the bracket at the twentieth ' // &
         'place that the kernel proves', re > lo_re .and. re < lo_re + w .and. im > lo_im .and. im < lo_im + w)
    call eta_own(2, 60, 0.5_qp, 2.0_qp, re2, im2)
    call eta_mach(2, 0.5_qp, 2.0_qp, rm, imm)
    dev8 = max(abs(re - rm), abs(im - imm)); dev60 = max(abs(re2 - rm), abs(im2 - imm))
    write(*,'(a,es9.2,a,es9.2)') '  inner limits, distance from the machine functions at 8 and at 60 inner terms: ', &
         dev8, '  ', dev60
    call check('VII: the inner limits: at sixty inner terms the series of the kernel are the functions of the ' // &
         'machine to twenty-five places', dev60 < 1.0e-25_qp .and. dev8 < 1.0e-4_qp)
    zo = newton(cmplx(0.75_qp, 14.0_qp, qp), 40, .true., 400, 1.0e-6_qp, 12)
    write(*,'(a,f15.12,a,f16.12)') '  first zero by the four series of the kernel alone, from 3/4 + 14i: ', &
         real(zo, qp), ' + i ', aimag(zo)
    call check('VII: the first zero, located from off the line by the four series of the kernel alone: real part ' // &
         'one half to nine places', abs(real(zo, qp) - 0.5_qp) < 1.0e-9_qp .and. &
         abs(eta_acc(zo, 40, .true., 400)) < 1.0e-9_qp)
    ok = .true.
    do i = 1, 3
      z(i) = newton(cmplx(0.75_qp, h0(i), qp), 60, .false., 0, 1.0e-15_qp, 20)
      write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a,f28.25,a,f29.25)') '  zero ', i, ', from 3/4 + ', nint(h0(i)), 'i: ', real(z(i), qp), &
           ' + i ', aimag(z(i))
      if (abs(real(z(i), qp) - 0.5_qp) >= 1.0e-24_qp) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('VII: three zeros located from starts off the line, no ordinate supplied: each real part one half ' // &
         'to twenty-four places', ok)
    call check('VII: read afterwards, the tables give the same three heights to twelve places', &
         all(abs(aimag(z) - tab) < 1.0e-12_qp))
    t1 = real(aimag(z(1)), dp)
    mm = [10000, 100000, 1000000]; ok = .true.
    do i = 1, 3
      call partial(0.5_dp, t1, mm(i), sre, sim)
      r(i) = sqrt(sre * sre + sim * sim) * sqrt(real(mm(i), dp))
      if (r(i) <= 0.45_dp .or. r(i) >= 0.55_dp) ok = .false.
    end do
    write(*,'(a,3f9.5)') '  at the located zero, |S_M| root M at M = 10^4, 10^5, 10^6: ', r
    call check('VII: at the located zero the plain partial sums fall to zero as one half over the root of M', ok)
    call partial(0.75_dp, t1, 1000000, sre, sim)
    off = sqrt(sre * sre + sim * sim)
    write(*,'(a,f9.5)') '  at 3/4, the same height, |S_M| at M = 10^6: ', off
    call check('VII: control, the same height off the line: the partial sums stay away from zero', off > 0.05_dp)
  end subroutine zeta_series
end program universal_seat_twin

### Force_Witness.lean

~~~~~lean file=Force_Witness.lean
/-
  Force_Witness.lean · PhysOS Proof PSP-FORCE-WITNESS-01 · the force-witness closure.
  Core Lean 4.19.0. No import, no sorry, no admit, no native_decide, no axiom declared.

  Least erasure is the final ninth-gate bit. A run of the substrate is the atomic witness that the closure was
  computed: a run whose flag is true proves that a run exists. The value at the actual zero set is the field of
  the act: keyed, given, free.

  PART ONE is copied from Inescapable_Capstone.lean, every definition and every law unchanged, with the lemmas
  they stand on: the chart, the configurations, the record, the act, the ninth gate, the deed.
  PART TWO is new: the atomic step, the ninth gate packed, the deed of the substrate, the free bit, the closure
  and its guard.

  THE FREE BIT. Every run leaves the value to the act. the_deed_forces_nothing is the seated law, and
  the_run_does_not_force_the_value states it at every run. It is the fourth conjunct of the closure.
-/

namespace ForceWitness

/-! ## PART ONE · The seated carriers and laws, copied unchanged -/

/-- A point is (d, t): d its offset from the line, t its height. The line is d = 0. -/
abbrev Point := Int × Int

/-- The fold: s ↦ 1 − s̄ on the offset chart, (d, t) ↦ (−d, t). -/
def fold (p : Point) : Point := (-p.1, p.2)

/-- The line: offset zero. -/
def onLine (p : Point) : Prop := p.1 = 0

/-- The registration: it keeps the height and forgets the side. -/
def reg (p : Point) : Point := (0, p.2)

/-- Integer negation is an involution, by the integer's constructors. -/
theorem neg_neg_free : ∀ d : Int, - -d = d := fun
  | Int.ofNat 0 => rfl
  | Int.ofNat (_ + 1) => rfl
  | Int.negSucc _ => rfl

/-- An integer equal to its own negation is zero, by the integer's constructors. -/
theorem neg_self_zero : ∀ d : Int, -d = d → d = 0 := fun
  | Int.ofNat 0, _ => rfl
  | Int.ofNat (_ + 1), h => Int.noConfusion h
  | Int.negSucc _, h => Int.noConfusion h

/-- The fold is an involution. -/
theorem fold_involutive (p : Point) : fold (fold p) = p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  show (- -d, t) = (d, t)
  rw [neg_neg_free d]

/-- THE CUT IS THE LINE: the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line. -/
theorem the_cut_is_the_line (p : Point) : fold p = p ↔ onLine p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  exact ⟨fun h => neg_self_zero d (congrArg Prod.fst h), fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩

/-- The registration lands on the line. -/
theorem reg_lands (p : Point) : onLine (reg p) := rfl

/-- The registration erases nothing at a point exactly when the point is on the line. -/
theorem reg_erases_nothing_iff (p : Point) : reg p = p ↔ onLine p := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
  exact ⟨fun h => (congrArg Prod.fst h).symm, fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩

/-- A configuration: a set of points. Closed: the fold carries it to itself. -/
abbrev Config := Point → Prop

def Closed (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → S (fold p)

/-- The value: every point of the configuration is on the line. -/
def Value (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → onLine p

/-- Least erasure: the registration leaves every point of the configuration unchanged. -/
def LeastErasure (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → reg p = p

/-- The record of a configuration: what the registration leaves. -/
def Rec (S : Config) (q : Point) : Prop := ∃ p, S p ∧ reg p = q

def SameRecord (S S' : Config) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec S q ↔ Rec S' q

/-- The registered world of a point and its pair world. -/
def registered (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = reg p

def pairWorld (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = p ∨ s = fold p

theorem pair_world_closed (p : Point) : Closed (pairWorld p) := fun _ hs =>
  match hs with
  | Or.inl e => Or.inr (congrArg fold e)
  | Or.inr e => Or.inl (e ▸ fold_involutive p)

/-- The registered world and the pair world leave one record. -/
theorem one_record (p : Point) : SameRecord (registered p) (pairWorld p) := fun q =>
  ⟨fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs]; rfl⟩,
   fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨reg p, rfl, by
      rw [← hq]
      exact match hs with
        | Or.inl e => by rw [e]; rfl
        | Or.inr e => by rw [e]; rfl⟩⟩

theorem registered_has_value (p : Point) : Value (registered p) := fun s hs => by
  rw [hs]; exact reg_lands p

theorem pair_world_lacks_value (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) : ¬ Value (pairWorld p) :=
  fun hv => h (hv p (Or.inl rfl))

/-- THE RECORD DECIDES NOTHING: for every point off the line, no reading that respects the record returns the
    value on both its registered world and its pair world. -/
theorem record_decides_nothing (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) (g : Config → Prop)
    (hg : ∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) :
    ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p))) :=
  fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => pair_world_lacks_value p h
    (h2.mp ((hg _ _ (one_record p)).mp (h1.mpr (registered_has_value p))))

/-- THE ACT. The bit is supplied once, in the open, as a field of a type: a closed configuration with least
    erasure at it. The field is the value supplied; the type makes the supply visible to every reader. -/
structure ActualZeros where
  zeros : Config
  closed : Closed zeros
  supply : LeastErasure zeros

/-- FROM THE ACT, THE VALUE. -/
theorem value_from_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : Value Z.zeros :=
  fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (Z.supply p hp)

def e (n i : Nat) : List Int := (List.range n).map (fun j => if j == i then 1 else 0)

def neg3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Bool × Bool × Bool := (!s.1, !s.2.1, !s.2.2)

def par3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Nat :=
  (if s.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.2 then 1 else 0)

/-- The orientation of a sign pattern, the determinant of its diagonal: −1 to the number of flips. -/
def orient (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Int := if par3 s % 2 == 0 then 1 else -1

/-- The ordered factor pairs of n, by first factor; the swap sends a to n / a. -/
def pairs (n : Nat) : List Nat := (List.range (n + 1)).filter (fun a => 0 < a && n % a == 0)

/-- The price of exported freedom in native units: temperature is energy per bit, so b bits cost b·T. -/
def price (T bits : Nat) : Nat := bits * T

/-- A finite configuration: the heights of its zeros on the line, and its off-line pairs, each an offset that is not
    zero and a height. -/
structure FinCfg where
  line : List Int
  pairs : List (Int × Int)
  offset_ne : ∀ q ∈ pairs, q.1 ≠ 0

/-- The erased bits of a finite configuration: one per off-line pair, two points registered to one. -/
def erased (F : FinCfg) : Nat := F.pairs.length

/-- The executed frame: a formal content and the bit of whether it ran. Reading the content is formal. -/
abbrev Exec (Q : Type) := Bool × Q

def ran {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) : Bool := s.1

/-- The nine: the eight sign patterns and one more. -/
abbrev Gate := Option (Bool × Bool × Bool)

/-- The fold on the nine: total negation on the eight; the ninth is its own partner. -/
def gfold : Gate → Gate
  | none => none
  | some s => some (neg3 s)

/-- THE SEAT IS THE NINTH: the fold of the nine fixes a gate exactly when the gate is the ninth. -/
theorem seat_is_the_ninth (g : Gate) : gfold g = g ↔ g = none := by
  cases g with
  | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩
  | some s =>
    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
    constructor
    · intro h; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> cases h
    · intro h; cases h

/-- The orientation of a pattern is never zero. -/
theorem orient_ne_zero (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient s ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide

/-- Total negation flips the orientation. -/
theorem orient_flips (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient (neg3 s) = -orient s := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl

/-- The carrier of the nine onto the chart: a pattern lands on the wall or the edge by its orientation, the ninth on
    the line. -/
def toChart (t : Int) : Gate → Point
  | none => (0, t)
  | some s => (orient s, t)

/-- The carrier is equivariant: the fold of the nine is carried onto the fold of the chart. -/
theorem gate_carrier_equivariant (t : Int) (g : Gate) : toChart t (gfold g) = fold (toChart t g) := by
  cases g with
  | none => rfl
  | some s => obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl

/-- And under every carrier that separates partners, only the ninth does. -/
theorem faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (c : Gate → Point) (eqv : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = fold (c g))
    (sep : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = c g → gfold g = g) (g : Gate) : onLine (c g) ↔ g = none := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (seat_is_the_ninth g).mp (sep g ((eqv g).trans ((the_cut_is_the_line (c g)).mpr h)))
  · intro h
    subst h
    have e : fold (c none) = c none := (eqv none).symm
    exact (the_cut_is_the_line (c none)).mp e

/-- The orientation carrier separates partners. -/
theorem orientation_carrier_separates (t : Int) (g : Gate) (h : toChart t (gfold g) = toChart t g) :
    gfold g = g := by
  cases g with
  | none => rfl
  | some s =>
    exact absurd (neg_self_zero (orient s) ((orient_flips s).symm.trans (congrArg Prod.fst h))) (orient_ne_zero s)

/-- A gate owes a bit when some target is odd at it: no even reading returns that target, and one supplied odd
    witness fixes it by one calibration bit. -/
def OwesBit (g : Gate) : Prop := ∃ d : Gate → Bool, d (gfold g) = !d g

/-- At the seat no bit is owed: nothing is odd at a fixed point. -/
theorem seat_owes_no_bit : ¬ OwesBit none := by
  intro ⟨d, h⟩
  have h' : d none = !d none := h
  cases hd : d none <;> rw [hd] at h' <;> cases h'

/-- Off the seat a bit is owed, at every one of the eight. -/
theorem off_seat_owes_a_bit (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : OwesBit (some s) := by
  refine ⟨fun g => decide (g = some s), ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide

/-- The registered orbit of a gate, as a finite configuration: the ninth is one point on the line; each of the eight
    is one off-line pair. -/
def gateCfg (t : Int) : Gate → FinCfg
  | none => ⟨[t], [], fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
  | some s => ⟨[], [(orient s, t)], fun q h => by
      cases h with
      | head => exact orient_ne_zero s
      | tail _ h' => nomatch h'⟩

/-- The heat of registering a gate is zero exactly at the ninth. -/
theorem gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (t : Int) (g : Gate) :
    price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none := by
  cases g with
  | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => Nat.zero_mul T⟩
  | some s =>
    constructor
    · intro h
      have h1 : 1 * T = 0 := h
      rw [Nat.one_mul] at h1
      exact absurd h1 (Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hT)
    · intro h; cases h

/-- THE NINTH GATE IS LEAST ERASURE. At a gate, five readings are one: it is the fold's fixed point; it lands on
    the line; registration erases nothing there (forget); its registration is free (pay); no bit is owed there
    (supply). Each holds exactly at the ninth. -/
theorem ninth_gate_is_least_erasure (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
    (gfold g = g ↔ g = none) ∧
    (onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none) ∧
    (reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ↔ g = none) ∧
    (price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none) ∧
    (¬ OwesBit g ↔ g = none) := by
  have hl : onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none :=
    faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (toChart t) (gate_carrier_equivariant t) (orientation_carrier_separates t) g
  refine ⟨seat_is_the_ninth g, hl, (reg_erases_nothing_iff (toChart t g)).trans hl,
          gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth T hT t g, ?_⟩
  cases g with
  | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => seat_owes_no_bit⟩
  | some s => exact ⟨fun h => absurd (off_seat_owes_a_bit s) h, fun h => by cases h⟩

/-- A RUN IS ITS OWN ATOMIC WITNESS, of the deed: a state that ran proves that a run exists. -/
theorem the_run_witnesses_a_run {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) : ∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true := by
  exact ⟨s, h⟩

/-- AND OF NOTHING ELSE: a fact that holds whatever the configuration, the deed included, forces no value. -/
theorem the_deed_forces_nothing (D : Prop) (hD : D) : ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D → Value S := by
  intro hall
  exact pair_world_lacks_value (1, 0) (fun e => by cases e) (hall _ (pair_world_closed (1, 0)) hD)


/-! ## PART TWO · The force-witness closure -/

/-- THE ATOMIC STEP: a witness with its check proves the existential it witnesses. -/
theorem witness_proves_exists {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (w : α) (h : P w) : ∃ x, P x := ⟨w, h⟩

/-- THE NINTH GATE, PACKED: a gate is the ninth exactly when all five readings hold of it. The five biconditionals
    of ninth_gate_is_least_erasure, bound into one. -/
theorem ninth_gate_pack (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
    g = none ↔
      (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g) := by
  have h := ninth_gate_is_least_erasure t T hT g
  constructor
  · intro e
    exact ⟨h.1.mpr e, h.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.2.mpr e⟩
  · intro hh
    exact h.1.mp hh.1

/-- The deed of the substrate: a run, and the fact that it ran. -/
structure SubstrateDeed (Q : Type) where
  run : Exec Q
  didRun : ran run = true

/-- THE FREE BIT. A run whose flag is true leaves the value free: by the run the value does not stand on every
    closed configuration. It is the_deed_forces_nothing read at the flag of the deed. A computation is a deed, and
    the value is the field of the act. -/
theorem the_run_does_not_force_the_value {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) :
    ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
  fun hall => the_deed_forces_nothing (ran s = true) h (fun S hS _ => hall S hS)

/-- THE FORCE-WITNESS CLOSURE. For a deed of the substrate, a term of the act, and any gate: the gate is the ninth
    exactly when it is the fold's fixed point, on the line, erased nothing, free to register at a positive
    temperature and owing no bit; the value holds on the field the act supplies; a run that ran exists; and the
    run leaves the value free. The fourth conjunct is the free bit. It is the implementation of the force. -/
theorem force_witness_closure {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros)
    (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
    (g = none ↔
      (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g)) ∧
    Value Z.zeros ∧
    (∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true) ∧
    ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
  ⟨ninth_gate_pack t T hT g,
   value_from_the_act Z,
   the_run_witnesses_a_run d.run d.didRun,
   the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩

/-- THE GUARD ON THE CLOSURE, the double defense restated: the value comes by the act; between the registered
    world and the pair world of a point off the line, every reading that respects the record leaves the value
    free; and the deed leaves it free. -/
theorem force_witness_guarded {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros) :
    Value Z.zeros ∧
    (∀ (p : Point), ¬ onLine p → ∀ (g : Config → Prop), (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
      ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p)))) ∧
    ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
  ⟨value_from_the_act Z,
   fun p h g hg => record_decides_nothing p h g hg,
   the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩

end ForceWitness

/-! ## The cones, pinned. Each line is the compiler's own; a drifted cone fails the compile. -/
/-- info: 'ForceWitness.neg_neg_free' does not depend on any axioms -/
#guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.neg_neg_free
/-- info: 'ForceWitness.neg_self_zero' does not depend on any axioms -/
#guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.neg_self_zero
/-- info: 'ForceWitness.fold_involutive' does not depend on any axioms -/

### Force_Witness_Twin.f90

~~~~~fortran file=Force_Witness_Twin.f90
! Force_Witness_Twin.f90 · twin of PhysOS Proof PSP-FORCE-WITNESS-01, the force-witness closure, executed.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off Force_Witness_Twin.f90
! Three checks, each beside a control that must fail. Run plain, the three checks pass and each control is shown
! to fail as it must: six lines, no failure. Run with the argument  control , each check runs with its defect
! planted and all three lines are red; the boot runs it so once and refuses the seat if any line stays green.
!   I   the ninth gate: on none and the eight sign patterns the five readings agree, and they hold only at none.
!       Control: the fixed-point reading dropped.
!   II  the act: on the 512 worlds least erasure and the value agree, and on every closed world of least erasure,
!       the supply of the act, the value holds. Control: an off-seat world supplied and the value demanded.
!   III the deed: a true flag yields an existent run and decides no value bit; the two partners of a pair share
!       one record slot, indexed once, and no one image is both. Control: a registration that keeps the side.
program force_witness_twin
  implicit none
  integer :: checks, fails
  logical :: ctl
  character(len=32) :: arg
  checks = 0; fails = 0
  call get_command_argument(1, arg)
  ctl = (trim(arg) == 'control')
  if (ctl) write(*,'(a)') ' CONTROL FLAG SET: each check runs with its defect planted; every line below must be red'
  call ninth_gate()
  call the_act()
  call the_deed()
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', checks, ',"failures":', fails, '}'
  if (fails > 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(label, ok)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: label
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    checks = checks + 1
    if (ok) then
      write(*,'(2a)') '  PASS  ', label
    else
      fails = fails + 1
      write(*,'(2a)') '  FAIL  ', label
    end if
  end subroutine check
  ! the chart: offsets -1, 0, 1 and heights 0, 1, 2; the fold reverses the offset; the registration forgets it,
  ! unless it is the registration of the control, which keeps the side
  pure function fold(p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [-p(1), p(2)]
  end function fold
  pure function reg(p, keep) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    logical, intent(in) :: keep
    integer :: q(2)
    if (keep) then
      q = p
    else
      q = [0, p(2)]
    end if
  end function reg
  pure logical function online(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    online = p(1) == 0
  end function online
  pure integer function idx(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    idx = p(2) * 3 + p(1) + 2
  end function idx
  pure function pt(i) result(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    integer :: p(2)
    p = [mod(i - 1, 3) - 1, (i - 1) / 3]
  end function pt
  ! the gates: 0 is none; 1 to 8 are the eight sign patterns, the three signs the bits of g - 1. The fold of a
  ! pattern reverses all three signs; the orientation is the parity of the pattern.
  pure integer function gfold(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    if (g == 0) then
      gfold = 0
    else
      gfold = 9 - g
    end if
  end function gfold
  pure integer function orient(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    orient = merge(1, -1, mod(popcnt(g - 1), 2) == 0)
  end function orient
  pure function tochart(t, g) result(p)
    integer, intent(in) :: t, g
    integer :: p(2)
    if (g == 0) then
      p = [0, t]
    else
      p = [orient(g), t]
    end if
  end function tochart
  ! the configuration of a gate: none is one point on the line and no pair, a pattern one pair and no line point;
  ! the erased bits are the pairs, and the price is one T to a bit
  pure integer function erased(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    erased = merge(0, 1, g == 0)
  end function erased
  pure integer function price(temp, bits)
    integer, intent(in) :: temp, bits
    price = bits * temp
  end function price
  ! a gate owes a bit when some labelling of the nine gates by one bit tells it from its fold: found by search
  pure logical function owes(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    integer :: m
    owes = .false.
    do m = 0, 511
      if (btest(m, gfold(g)) .neqv. btest(m, g)) owes = .true.
    end do
  end function owes
  subroutine ninth_gate()
    integer :: g, t, temp, nag, nagc
    logical :: r(5), rc(5)
    nag = 0; nagc = 0
    do g = 0, 8
      do t = 0, 2
        do temp = 1, 3
          r(1) = gfold(g) == g
          r(2) = online(tochart(t, g))
          r(3) = all(reg(tochart(t, g), .false.) == tochart(t, g))
          r(4) = price(temp, erased(g)) == 0
          r(5) = .not. owes(g)
          if (all(r .eqv. (g == 0))) nag = nag + 1
          rc = r; rc(1) = .true.
          if (all(rc .eqv. (g == 0))) nagc = nagc + 1
        end do
      end do
    end do
    if (.not. ctl) then
      call check('I: on none and the eight sign patterns, at three heights and three temperatures, the five ' // &
           'readings agree, and they hold only at none', nag == 81)
      call check('I: control, the fixed-point reading dropped: the agreement fails on the eight sign patterns', &
           nagc == 9)
    else
      call check('I: [defect planted: the fixed-point reading dropped] the five readings agree on every gate', &
           nagc == 81)
    end if
  end subroutine ninth_gate
  ! worlds: the 512 subsets of the nine points, a bit to a point
  pure logical function member(m, i)
    integer, intent(in) :: m, i
    member = btest(m, i - 1)
  end function member
  pure logical function closed(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: i
    closed = .true.
    do i = 1, 9
      if (member(m, i) .and. .not. member(m, idx(fold(pt(i))))) closed = .false.
    end do
  end function closed
  pure logical function lerase(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: i
    lerase = .true.
    do i = 1, 9
      if (member(m, i) .and. .not. all(reg(pt(i), .false.) == pt(i))) lerase = .false.
    end do
  end function lerase
  pure logical function valu(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: i
    valu = .true.
    do i = 1, 9
      if (member(m, i) .and. .not. online(pt(i))) valu = .false.
    end do
  end function valu
  pure integer function recmask(m, keep)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    logical, intent(in) :: keep
    integer :: i
    recmask = 0
    do i = 1, 9
      if (member(m, i)) recmask = ibset(recmask, idx(reg(pt(i), keep)) - 1)
    end do
  end function recmask
  subroutine the_act()
    integer :: m, nag, nsup, nval, zs
    nag = 0; nsup = 0; nval = 0
    do m = 0, 511
      if (lerase(m) .eqv. valu(m)) nag = nag + 1
      if (closed(m) .and. lerase(m)) then
        nsup = nsup + 1
        if (valu(m)) nval = nval + 1
      end if
    end do
    zs = ior(ibset(0, idx([1, 0]) - 1), ibset(0, idx([-1, 0]) - 1))
    if (.not. ctl) then
      call check('II: on the 512 worlds least erasure and the value agree; on each of the 8 closed worlds of ' // &
           'least erasure, the supply of the act, the value holds', nag == 512 .and. nsup == 8 .and. nval == 8)
      call check('II: control, an off-seat world supplied and the value demanded: closed, no world of least ' // &
           'erasure, and the demand fails', closed(zs) .and. .not. lerase(zs) .and. .not. valu(zs))
    else
      call check('II: [defect planted: an off-seat world supplied as the act] the value holds on the supplied ' // &
           'world', closed(zs) .and. lerase(zs) .and. valu(zs))
    end if
  end subroutine the_act
  subroutine the_deed()
    logical :: flags(3), exists, keep, onerec, split
    integer :: p(2), q(2), ip, iq, r, rq, v, v2, nboth1, none1, ntwo, wa, wb, c, nflag
    flags = [.false., .true., .false.]
    exists = any(flags)
    keep = ctl
    p = [1, 0]; q = fold(p); ip = idx(p); iq = idx(q)
    wa = ibset(0, idx(reg(p, .false.)) - 1)
    wb = ior(ibset(0, ip - 1), ibset(0, iq - 1))
    onerec = recmask(wa, keep) == recmask(wb, keep)
    split = valu(wa) .neqv. valu(wb)
    ! a reading of the flag returns one bit, the same on both worlds: it is the value on at most one of them
    nflag = 0
    do c = 0, 1
      if (((c == 1) .eqv. valu(wa)) .and. ((c == 1) .eqv. valu(wb))) nflag = nflag + 1
    end do
    ! the record slot of each partner, indexed once; then the one image a map can give the one slot
    r = idx(reg(p, keep)); rq = idx(reg(q, keep))
    nboth1 = 0; none1 = 0
    do v = 1, 9
      if (v == ip .and. v == iq) nboth1 = nboth1 + 1
      if (v == ip .or. v == iq) none1 = none1 + 1
    end do
    ! under a registration that keeps the side the partners hold two slots, and a map gives each its own image
    ntwo = 0
    do v = 1, 9
      do v2 = 1, 9
        if (v == ip .and. v2 == iq) ntwo = ntwo + 1
      end do
    end do
    if (.not. ctl) then
      write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a,i0,a,i0)') '  record slots of the partners ', r, ' and ', rq, &
           '; images equal to both partners ', nboth1, ' of 9; to one of them ', none1
      call check('III: the flag is true and a run exists; over one record the registered world and the pair ' // &
           'world part on the value and no reading of the flag returns it on both; the partners share one ' // &
           'slot and no one image is both', exists .and. onerec .and. split .and. nflag == 0 .and. r == rq &
           .and. ip /= iq .and. nboth1 == 0 .and. none1 == 2)
      call check('III: control, a registration that keeps the side: the partners hold two slots and one pair ' // &
           'of images recovers both', idx(reg(p, .true.)) /= idx(reg(q, .true.)) .and. ntwo == 1 .and. &
           recmask(wa, .true.) /= recmask(wb, .true.))
    else
      call check('III: [defect planted: a registration that keeps the side] the two partners share one ' // &
           'record slot and the two worlds share one record', onerec .and. r == rq)
    end if
  end subroutine the_deed
end program force_witness_twin
